title: Scipion de Gonzague (Français 4696); not established for Français 4698 to Duke of Nevers (Français 4696); not established for Français 4698, 1585–1589 (Français 4696); 1590 (Français 4698) (Français 4696 / 4698 — graphical cipher, ff5r/62r–v, ff30r– 31r and f104r)

steps.what: George Lasry (with ChatGPT Astra 6 and Anthropic Opus 5.5) transcribed and deciphered the item: 2/7 pages transcribed; 5 more in part; 7/7 pages deciphered in part; 3,078 recorded groups, 1,147 identified; 8 further groups with unresolved boundaries. Report section: see report.

Spot-check against the Gallica image (https://gallica.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/btv1b9059540q/f127.item): Fr. 4696 f62r: Italian letter "Ill.mo et Ecc.mo S. mio" with clear text (Padre Toledo, Giulio Cesare, Pasqua) and Greek-like graphic cipher runs; excerpt is from f62v, not imaged here; sign-level decode with his table not completed (glyph forms at this scan only loosely match his crops) Verdict: partly confirmed.
Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): linked George Lasry's report excerpt (lasry_entry.md); his full transcription and decryption are not in the repository

texts.summary: Scipion de Gonzague to the Duke of Nevers, 1585-1589 (BnF fr. 4696), and a letter of 1590 by an unestablished writer (fr. 4698). Confidential warnings and cavalry arrangements: horses, payments, dispatches and service in war. The fr. 4698 fragment contains a request for an appeal or intercession, and the Paris letter of 16 February 1590 discusses friendship, the King of Spain and a request; most of both remains unread.
texts.note: The repository holds only the excerpt and translation in George Lasry's report (lasry_entry.md); his full transcription and decryption are his and not yet in the repository, and the ciphertext has not been transcribed here.
